doc.p: Exact: every line of this paragraph is fourteen points high whatever its text holds, even where a larger word stands in it, and the baseline sits the font's descent above the line's foot.
At least: a line is as high as its tallest font sets solid, where that is more than the line spacing; a larger word makes its line taller, the next lines are as high as the spacing asks.
With leading: two points between lines of the natural height, a larger word included, and nothing else changes in the text that runs on to fill more than one line of the page.
After the baseline: min-post-line-spacing asks for five points below every placement path, more than the descent of the text, and the rest of the spacing lies above it, so the text moves up.
Before the baseline: min-pre-line-spacing asks for eleven points above every placement path, and what the line has more lies below it, so the text moves down in its line.
Shifted: a raised superscript and a lowered subscript stand on their own placement paths, and the line reaches as far down as the lowered one does.

The page ends here: this paragraph is long enough to run over the foot of the page, so the line that does not fit begins the next page at its top, and the space before it is dropped there because it does not belong to the new page. More text follows to make sure of it, and more, and more again, line after line after line.
